Physics Graduate Program
Application Requirements
Students with a bachelor’s degree in physics or a closely related area are prepared to begin graduate studies in physics at Lehigh and are encouraged to apply. Students with degrees in related areas will also be considered; their graduate programs will be designed to make up for possible deficiencies in physics or mathematics preparation.
Admissions Standards
We seek academically prepared and motivated students for our graduate program. Applicants with an academic record that included advanced courses in physics and mathematics are ready for graduate-level classes and research. In the evaluation process we review all details of the application, including performance in individual math and science classes, and the ability to grapple with complex quantitative questions. We review all elements of an application to understand a student’s prior accomplishments and capability to carry out graduate-level original research in physics. We seek students from a range of backgrounds and perspectives to contribute to a diverse and inclusive departmental culture. Prior experience in scientific research is a benefit, but we realize that not all undergraduates have equal access to such opportunities.
We seek well-prepared students for both the master’s program and the PhD program, although the admissions criteria are not the same for both. Students who are admitted to the MS program may choose to apply to the PhD program once they have completed their master’s work, and they will be considered for admission to the PhD program together with all the other applicants.
International Applicants
Our graduate program follows the College of Arts and Sciences English Language Proficiency Policy. This policy lists the accepted tests, minimum scores, score-validity requirements, and alternative ways to demonstrate English proficiency.
Students appointed as teaching assistants may also be required to complete an English-language assessment through Lehigh’s International Center for Academic and Professional English.
For information about visas and immigration, visit the Office of International Students and Scholars.
Items that must be submitted with an application
Applications must be submitted on-line. The application requires the following materials:
A completed application form, including the applicant’s contact information, curriculum vitae, personal statement, and other information.
Transcripts from each college or university attended. Unofficial transcripts are acceptable for application review; official transcripts will be required before matriculation. Documents not issued in English must be accompanied by an English translation.
Three letters of recommendation. Applicants enter the names and email addresses of their recommenders in the online application. After the application is submitted, each recommender will receive an automated email with instructions for submitting a letter.
A $50 non-refundable application fee.
Evidence of English-language proficiency, if applicable. Applicants should consult the current College of Arts and Sciences English Language Proficiency Policy for accepted tests, minimum scores, and alternative ways of satisfying this requirement. English-language test scores are valid for two years and must remain valid until an I-20 is issued. Unofficial scores are acceptable for application review, but official scores are required before matriculation.
International applicants admitted to the terminal MS program must provide proof of sufficient financial support before enrollment. This requirement does not apply to PhD students who receive financial support from the Physics Department. Students admitted only to the terminal MS program are not eligible for departmental teaching assistantships, research assistantships, or fellowships.
GRE scores are optional but encouraged
The GRE General Test and the Physics GRE Subject Test are optional; neither is required for admission to the Physics MS or PhD programs. The Physics Department encourages applicants to the PhD program to submit scores from both tests when available. The Graduate Admissions Committee will consider GRE scores as one component of the complete application.
Official GRE scores are not required for initial application review. Applicants who choose to submit GRE scores must also provide a copy of their score report showing their full name, test date, and scores. Applicants who are admitted and enroll must submit official scores.
Application Deadline
The Physics Department’s full-consideration deadline for Fall admission is January 15 of each year. Applications completed by this date will receive full consideration. Later applications may be considered if space and funding remain. When applying late, contact us directly to discuss your situation.
